text: In 2023, UNComtrade shows Canada imported 3,000 kg of cadmium from the United States, 3,000 kg from Germany, 1,000 kg from Peru, and smaller amounts from several other countries. USGS reports Canada produced 1.7 kt of refined cadmium in 2024 and 1.8 kt of refined cadmium in 2023, which may indicate significant Canadian production of primary or secondary cadmium (U.S. Geological Survey 2025e). • Tellurium: According to USGS, 60% of global tellurium consumed in 2024 was for PV applications, followed by thermoelectric devices (20%) and metallurgy (15%) (U.S. Geological Survey 2025n). The HTS code for tellurium is 2804.50.0020 (purity not specified). Figure 43 shows U.S. export and import data. For each year shown, Canada represents most exports and imports, although amounts vary significantly. Exports reported under this code may include copper telluride (the intermediate compound refined from copper slimes before further processing into purified tellurium) (U.S. Geological Survey 2025n). UNComtrade only reports trade data for the HS code 2804.50, which includes o both boron and tellurium. In 2024, UNComtrade shows Canada imported 0.4 kt from China under this code, followed by 0.2 kt from South Korea, and less from any other country (United Nations 2025). However, most of this may represent boron, because global production of boron appears to exceed global production of tellurium (U.S. Geological Survey 2025s). The estimated amount of tellurium needed per GW of CdTe PV modules is 46 t o dc (46 mg/W). As of 2025, global reserves of tellurium are estimated at 35,000 t (U.S. Geological Survey 2025n), which could supply 760 GW of CdTe modules. dc However, the rate at which these reserves can be extracted cost-effectively is limited by their production as a byproduct of copper refining. Global production of tellurium was estimated to be about 944 t in 2023 and 980 t in 2024 (U.S. Geological Survey 2025n). While future global production of tellurium may vary, reserves appear sufficient to support 30 years of annual production equivalent to 25 GW of CdTe modules. dc • Selenium: In 2024, 40% of global selenium consumed was for metallurgy, including manganese production, followed by 20% for agriculture and animal health, 20% for glass manufacturing, 10% for electronics and PV, and 5% for chemicals and pigments (U.S. Geological Survey 2025l). The HTS code for selenium is 2804.90.0000, and U.S. export and import data are shown in Figure 44. • Zinc: Most zinc in 2024 was used to produce galvanized steel, followed by brass and bronze and other zinc-base alloys (U.S. Geological Survey 2025q).
